title: Ranking QC pairwise manifest and slice notes (2026)
body:
Purpose:
This is the working manifest and QC playbook for the next reranking onboarding evaluation. Intended consumers: applied-ml engineers, labeling ops, and solutions engineers doing regression signoffs. The focus is pairwise preference labeling + downstream conversion to graded relevance for NDCG reporting, plus slice-level analysis and simple QC heuristics.

Dataset summary (target and sources):
- Target: 18,000 pairwise judgments covering ~3,500 unique queries, targeted to produce stable per-slice NDCG estimates.
- Pairwise budget: avg 5 independent votes per pair (primary label + 4 checks).
- Sources: production search logs (sampled by frequency), recent failing queries from error-tracking (tickets linked), synthetic perturbations (typoed queries, paraphrase generation).
- Split: 80% sampling from realistic logs, 10% adversarial/long-tail, 10% synthetic/edge cases.

Sampling strategy and quotas (practical):
- Stratify on query frequency: High (top 5k queries) / Medium / Tail. Ensure at least 600 tail queries represented.
- Force-at-least-one for regression-sensitive queries: any query in last 90d with delta-NDCG > 0.02 between current prod and candidate must be included.
- Pair construction: for each query sample top-K documents from baseline and candidate model, then pair across models and within model (to capture intra-model reordering). Limit pair distance to <=10 rank positions for majority of pairs; include a small fraction (5%) long-distance swaps (>20 positions).

Labeling instructions (to annotators):
- Label types: 'A' means docA preferred to docB; 'B' means docB preferred; 'T' means tie/indistinguishable.
- Optional fields: confidence (1-5), short rationale (1-2 sentence).
- Preference guidelines: prefer answer completeness first, then factual correctness, then fluency. For multi-turn/chat snippets, prefer relevance to the final user intent.
- Edge rules: when both are equally relevant but one is more concise, mark preference for concision only if brevity materially improves answer quality.
- Toy examples (annotator-facing):
  - Query: 'best laptop for video editing under 1000'
    docA: focused on GPUs & benchmarks (prefer A) -> label A
  - Query: 'how to boil an egg'
    docA: long tutorial with steps; docB: 1-sentence answer but missing timing (prefer A) -> label A
  - Query: ambiguous intent where both plausible answers present -> label T and add note.

Adjudication policy and IAA targets:
- Each pair receives 3 primary labels + 2 adjudicators if disagreement (majority wins). For persistent ties, escalate to senior reviewer.
- Inter-annotator agreement target: Cohen's kappa >= 0.55 on the sample audit; Krippendorff alpha > 0.6 desirable.
- Consensus label mapping: majority A/B/T; if no majority, mark as 'ambiguous' and exclude from graded-relevance conversion unless senior adjudicated.

Converting pairwise votes to graded relevance for NDCG:
We need graded relevance per document per query. We use a two-step approach: aggregate pairwise preferences into a Bradley-Terry score per document, then map scores into discrete relevance bins (0..3) for DCG.
Steps:
1) For each query, collect all pairwise votes involving documents for that query.
2) Fit a simple Bradley-Terry model (log-odds) to produce a real-valued score s_d for each doc d. Implementation note: for small per-query doc sets (<=10), use an L2-regularized BT fit; if fit fails (insufficient comparisons), fall back to counting wins/(wins+losses).
3) Normalize s_d to [0,1] using min-max per query; then map to relevance bins: [0,0.2)=>0, [0.2,0.45)=>1, [0.45,0.75)=>2, [0.75,1.0]=>3. We chose these thresholds after small pilot; they can be tuned.
4) Compute DCG@k using standard formula: DCG = sum_{i=1..k} (2^{rel_i}-1)/log2(i+1). IDCG is DCG of ideal ordering by rel. NDCG = DCG/IDCG.

Numeric example (illustrative):
- Query q1 has 3 documents with aggregated rels: doc1=3, doc2=2, doc3=1. Candidate ranking = [doc2, doc1, doc3]. Compute DCG@3 for candidate:
  - rels at ranks: [2,3,1]
  - DCG = (2^2-1)/log2(1+1) + (2^3-1)/log2(2+1) + (2^1-1)/log2(3+1)
  - DCG = (3)/1 + (7)/1.585 + (1)/2 = 3 + 4.42 + 0.5 = 7.92
  - IDCG (ideal [3,2,1]) = (7)/1 + (3)/1.585 + (1)/2 = 7 + 1.89 + 0.5 = 9.39
  - NDCG = 7.92/9.39 = 0.843
Notes: include these per-query examples in final eval report to help reviewers validate the pipeline.

Slice definitions and analysis plan:
We will compute per-slice aggregated metrics (mean delta NDCG, pairwise error rate, percent ties) and produce visualizations (ecdf of per-query delta NDCG, waterfall of top regression queries). Candidate slices:
- Intent length: short (<=3 tokens), medium (4-7), long (>7).
- Entity-rich: queries with 2+ named entities (NER heuristics).
- Conversational context: multi-turn queries (presence of 'follow-up' tokens).
- Answer-type: factual, definitional, procedural, opinion (classification model).
- Low-similarity: baseline embedding cosine < 0.2 to returned doc.
- Long-distance swaps: pairs where rank distance > 10 in baseline vs candidate.
Per-slice thresholds to flag: mean delta NDCG <= -0.015 AND at least 50 queries in slice => fail signal. Also monitor percent of queries with NDCG drop > 0.05.

Regression reporting checklist (for signoff):
- Baseline and candidate models identified (model ids + date).
- Global summary: mean delta NDCG@10, median delta NDCG, percent queries improved/worse.
- Significance: run paired Wilcoxon test on per-query NDCG deltas; require p < 0.01 for claiming improvement. Also produce bootstrap CI for mean delta.
- Per-slice table: for each slice include mean delta, count, p-value, flagged boolean.
- Top 25 failing queries with annotator notes attached.
- Runtime/latency checks: reranking latency percentile differences should be < 10% relative.

QC checks and label sanity heuristics:
- Sanity: ensure label distributions are not >90% A or B; extreme skew suggests broken pair generation.
- Duplicate pairs: dedupe by canonical doc ids.
- Anchor pairs: include 200 gold pairs (pre-labeled by SMEs) mixed into labeling batches to monitor labeler accuracy (target acc > 88%).
- Worker-level drift: compute per-annotator agreement against gold anchors; flag annotators < 0.7 accuracy for review.

Manifest/CSV specification (columns for labeling tool and archival):
- query_id, query_text, docA_id, docA_url, docA_snippet, docB_id, docB_url, docB_snippet, baseline_rank_docA, baseline_rank_docB, candidate_rank_docA, candidate_rank_docB, pair_id, label, confidence, annotator_id, created_at, note
Example row (CSV-like):
- q_20260217_001, "how to crop a video on mac", d_993, "https://.../d_993", "Open QuickTime -> File -> Trim", d_1021, "https://.../d_1021", "use iMovie for fine edits", 1, 3, 2, 1, p_0001, A, 4, ann_007, 2026-02-18, "A more complete step-by-step"

Reporting dashboards and deliverables:
- Per-query export (CSV) for deep-dive.
- Aggregate dashboard: time series and slice heatmap (Redwood Console prototype + small Looker dashboard).
- PDF regression brief with top failing queries and labeler rationales for product review.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm BT implementation choice: Python bt-utilities vs custom SGD; Diego to prototype and report runtime on 3.5k queries.
- Thresholds for rel-bin mapping need calibration on pilot of 2k pairs (Priya).
- Decide whether to include pairwise ties in IDCG computation or drop tied docs (affects NDCG). Current plan: include ties but map to same rel bin.
- Automate per-slice bootstrapping in evaluation pipeline (Zoe to add unit tests).

Notes to self:
- Keep labeling batches small (<=100 pairs) to reduce annotator fatigue.
- Add an explicit step in pipeline to log model commit hash next to dataset for reproducibility.

Slack links for context: #applied-ml, thread ML-4123 (sampling debate), and attached pilot labeling spreadsheet in Google Drive (shared with labeling ops).

End of working doc. This will be iterated after pilot run (expected 2026-03-07).
